correctness.rationale: Transposing the consecutive values j and j+1 bijects the fair J_j conditions. At other positions comparisons with j and j+1 agree, and at the earlier swapped position all prefix comparisons against the earlier maximum agree. At the later position a record is lost, never gained, precisely when the first two high labels in {j,…,n} are j,j+1 in that order. For m=n−j+1 that conditional fraction is (m−2)!/(m!/2)=2/[m(m−1)], with a change only at T_2, the second high position. High positions are a uniform m-subset independently of high-label order; exactly (i−1) binom(n−i,m−2) subsets have T_2=i. The conditional difference multiplied by −1/4 gives the stated binomial covariance after cancelling factorials. Its support is 2≤i≤j+1 and its diagonal i=j+1 is strictly negative. Summing T_2 probabilities gives the column total and summing 1/[h(h+1)] gives both telescoping identities. At n=2 the pair of indicators are complementary; R_1 is deterministic in all sizes. Domination is for one fixed J_j, not joint negative association or an equality for total-variation distance. Inspected the frozen checker, not run: it asserts the exact covariance entries and per-swap change pattern on a finite range, not a separate closed-form mismatch-probability total. The latter follows from the label-order argument.

value.rationale: The coupling orders every increasing functional of the record vector under one inverse-descent condition, which is stronger than pairwise covariance signs. The triangular full-rank kernel and exact localization at the highest value ranks reveal how the known aggregate dependence arises, with a specific mechanism absent from the aggregate count statistic.
